subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should the remaining Slack latency work be resolved by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted transport, or by changing Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the measured remaining delay is mostly outside OpenClaw code, but steering or changing Slack setup affects new deployment expectations and public-ingress requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger Slack setup/default change that steers hosted installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the current transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurement and merged the partial Slack fixes while explicitly leaving this HTTP guidance decision as the follow-up.
